A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoH research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables, figures, prompts, and code examples. Corresponding material can be matched despite reorganization and expanded evaluation.

before.justification: v1 reports original TSP and online BPP experiments, ablations, and computational-cost measurements, with TSPLIB, CVRP, and offline BPP results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds distribution-shift evaluation, mixed-problem training, statistical analyses, and QAP and Acrobot results.

M1.justification: The two-level optimization procedure, Algorithm 1, population management, prompt templates, and displayed heuristic and optimizer code retain their substantive operations. Renaming optimizers as heuristic-optimizers and specifying previously unspecified task weights clarify the method without establishing an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: v2 adds QAP facility-layout optimization and Acrobot robotic control evaluations in Appendix C.7, substantially extending task and domain coverage. Appendix A also adds clustered-TSP evaluation after uniform-distribution training. CVRP and offline BPP were already evaluated in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: v2 adds ReEvo-GLS to Table 1, SIL to both TSPLIB comparisons, and LEHD to the larger-instance TSPLIB comparison. The new solver-time comparison includes NeuOpt and SIL, while Table 14 adds EoH and HSEvo to comparisons across LLMs that previously evaluated MoH alone. These materially broaden evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include joint training across TSP-GLS, TSP-KGLS, and online BPP; approximately matched solving-time comparisons, except for unconstrained Concorde; and evaluation over 100 Acrobot initial conditions and 128 QAP instances. A TSP100 cost experiment supplements the retained TSP200 experiment. The original main-experiment budgets remain unchanged; the newly explained TSPLIB selection procedure is a disclosure rather than an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: v2 adds uniform-to-cluster transfer testing, a mixed-problem training probe, comparative robustness analysis across four LLMs, and expanded computational-cost and solving-time analyses. These examine generalization boundaries, dependence on the LLM, and practical efficiency. The original population-size and idea-generation ablations and optimizer case studies are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports best-of-three results and three-run averages without corresponding uncertainty estimates. v2 adds five-run means with standard errors in Table 6, five-run means with standard deviations in Table 14, further mean-and-standard-deviation results in Table 16, and one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests in Table 15. Existing three-run results remain alongside these additions.

E6.justification: Shared entries in Tables 1 and 2, the original TSPLIB comparisons, and the relocated CVRP/offline BPP table retain their values. Substantial new results include comparator scores, runtime measurements, repeated-run summaries, and additional tasks. For example, Table 7 reports clustered-TSP gaps of 0.268% for MoH versus 0.290% for ReEvo; Table 17 reports Acrobot steps of 88.76 versus 99.65. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.1 adds an explicit mathematical definition of the previously unspecified task weights: wi = si / sum_j sj, where si is task size. The two optimization objectives and existing problem constraints remain substantively unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The principal claims about optimizer-level search, multi-task training, and strong cross-size performance remain. The novelty claim is modestly qualified: the introduction replaces discovering novel optimization strategies with discovering effective strategies, and Appendix A explicitly says that novelty of the generated meta-optimizers themselves is not emphasized.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly distinguishes cross-size generalization from direct cross-problem transfer and acknowledges difficulties using one meta-optimizer across structurally different problems. It also explains size weighting and the distinction from prompt optimization. New cost analyses argue that heuristic evaluation dominates runtime and discuss deployment tradeoffs. Some new superiority interpretations overreach: Table 14 includes settings where HSEvo outperforms MoH.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code repository address where v1 only promised future code and dataset release; the PDF establishes the access claim, not independently verified availability. It also specifies size-based task weights and discloses instance-wise selection among size-specific heuristics for TSPLIB, applied to baselines as well. Additional runtime, token, request, and evaluation-count measurements expand resource documentation.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially develops positioning relative to evolutionary multitasking, multi-objective optimization, bilevel optimization, and meta-prompt optimization, adding references including Gupta, Osaba, Gunantara, and Xu. The related-work survey is also condensed: its separate heatmap-guided category and several citations disappear, while references supporting SIL and LLM4AD are added. These changes go beyond relocating related work or updating citation style.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes the narrative by moving main-text related work into Appendix B, bringing existing CVRP/offline BPP material forward, and adding an extensive FAQ and appendix contents page. Terminology is revised throughout to distinguish heuristic-optimizers from meta-optimizers, with expanded explanations of their roles. The title, author block, and publication headers also change.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn with explicit populations, prompt examples, and illustrated utility aggregation. New evaluation and statistics tables expand the presentation; existing tables gain comparator rows or columns, and the CVRP/offline BPP table moves into the main text. The conference formatting also reorganizes figures, tables, and appendix code displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence beyond v1's best-of-three headline results through variability reporting, significance analyses, broader comparator coverage, and targeted generalization tests. Explicit cross-problem limitations and the disclosed TSPLIB selection procedure also improve interpretability and reproducibility. Some new claims remain overstated: Table 14 reports HSEvo beating MoH with Qwen-plus at TSP1000, contrary to its accompanying claim of consistently lower errors. Nevertheless, the added evidence and methodological transparency provide a substantial net improvement.
